items.title: SYNTHETIC: counting equal lots
items.core_explanation_md: This is **engineering test material**, not exam content. When every lot holds the same number of units, the total is the number of lots multiplied by the size of one lot. Three lots of four units hold twelve units. Adding the two numbers instead (3 + 4) is the usual slip: it counts a lot and a unit as if they were the same thing.
items.expanded_explanation_md:
Multiplication is repeated addition of equal groups: 4 + 4 + 4 is the same as 3 × 4. The order does not change the total, so three lots of four and four lots of three both hold twelve units.

- Check that the lots really are equal before multiplying.
- Keep the unit with the answer: lots × units per lot = units.

self_check.prompt_text: Without looking, say how you would find the total units in 6 equal lots of 7 units, and name the common slip.
self_check.expected_takeaway: Multiply lots by lot size: 6 × 7 = 42 units. The slip is adding the two numbers (13).

items.title: SYNTHETIC rule: Test Tray Handling Rule 4(2)(b)
items.core_explanation_md: A made-up rule used to test long statutory layouts. Under this fictional rule, a tray may be released only when at least 60% of its units have been counted twice. It has no connection to any real law or regulation.

statute_spec.act_or_direction_name: SYNTHETIC Test Tray Handling Rules (fictional, for layout testing only)
statute_spec.section_or_clause: Rule 4(2)(b) read with the Explanation to Rule 4(3)
statute_spec.rule_summary: A tray is releasable when the number of units counted twice is at least 60% of all units on the tray, measured at the close of the counting session in which the second count was completed.
statute_spec.applicability: Applies to every fictional tray holding more than 10 units; smaller trays follow the fictional Rule 5.
exceptions: Trays marked "sample" are exempt from the second count.
A tray recounted because of a spill restarts its percentage from zero for that session.
thresholds_or_penalties: A tray released below the threshold must be recalled within 2 counting sessions.

items.title: SYNTHETIC: flat growth
items.core_explanation_md: Test material only. Flat growth adds the same amount every period: the amount added is the starting quantity multiplied by the rate and by the number of periods. Nothing is added on top of earlier growth.

assumptions: The rate is constant for every period.
Growth is never added to the base.
common_errors: Using the rate as a whole number instead of dividing by 100.
Mixing months and years for r and t.

items.title: SYNTHETIC: repeated growth, step by step
items.core_explanation_md: Test material only. Repeated growth applies the rate to the grown quantity each period. A quantity of 20,000 units grows at 8% a year, applied four times a year, for 2 years.

worked_steps.description: Find the rate for one period.
Multiply the starting quantity by the factor.

self_check.prompt_text: Why is the result larger than flat growth at the same rate and time?
self_check.expected_takeaway: Each period's growth is added to the base, so later periods grow a larger quantity.

items.title: SYNTHETIC case: the practice storeroom
items.scenario_narrative_md: TEST ONLY. A practice storeroom keeps two bins. **Bin A** starts with 8,000 units and grows flat at 5% per period. **Bin B** starts with 8,000 units and grows at 5% per period applied to the grown quantity. The storekeeper also packs finished units into equal lots of 25 units, and releases a shelf only when at least 60% of its lots have been checked. This week a shelf holds 40 lots, of which 26 have been checked. Each question below can be answered from this scenario alone; none depends on an earlier answer.
reference_tables_md:
| Bin | Start (units) | Rate per period | Growth applies to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 8,000 | 5% | Starting quantity only |
| B | 8,000 | 5% | Grown quantity |

| Shelf fact | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Lots on shelf | 40 |
| Lots checked | 26 |
| Units per lot | 25 |
